headline: UK-based Universal Quantum raised more than $100 million to scale up quantum computers built from many linked chips.
score_reason: Large round for a European quantum company; the claims about scale come from the company and its investors.
importance_line: A UK firm with a $77 million German Aerospace Center contract is getting private backing for a different route to large quantum machines, which matters to European research buyers and rival builders, but the design is not shown working at full scale and the record claim is the company's own.
summary: Universal Quantum announced in a press release, carried by The Quantum Insider, that its Series A round, co-led by DCVC and Firgun Ventures, passed $100 million, which the company calls the largest Series A ever raised by a UK-headquartered quantum firm. The money will fund its modular design, in which many small trapped-ion chips (charged atoms used as qubits) are linked together, and a new research centre in Singapore.
notes: Press release text carried by The Quantum Insider; the round is also reported by SiliconANGLE.
